_doc: C21 — ONE SEMANTICS, MANY TRANSPORTS, MANY RUNTIMES. The canonical assertion (a2a-tck ALL_TRANSPORTS, openai-agents runtime-symmetry): the SAME envelope, sent through ANY transport to ANY runtime, yields the SAME reply. Cases are DATA — add one here and every transport in every runtime is on the hook for it, with no per-runtime test to forget. JSON, not YAML, so every runtime reads it with what it already has: node parses it natively (the ts kernel ships ZERO runtime deps), python via json, rust via serde_json, swift via its own JSON type. JSON is also valid YAML, so a yaml parser reads it unchanged.
_root_placeholder: `$root` in an `expect` means THAT RUNTIME'S root id — python `kernel_state`, rust/swift `core`. Parity asserts the per-runtime value, never equality. The target `kernel` is the alias every runtime resolves to its own root.
_fixture: Built by each driver: `c21_probe` — an agent answering `poke` with {poked:<value>} and `reflect` with {id, sentence, verbs}; every transport leg granted on it. `c21_nobody` never exists.
_order: Cases replay IN ORDER against ONE kernel per leg, and a driver that compares legs pairwise replays the whole list per leg. So a case that MUTATES state must come FIRST and be idempotent — otherwise the legs after it observe a tree the first leg did not, and every later record-reading case (`list-agents-limited`) diverges for a reason that has nothing to do with the transport. `update-agent-shape` is the one mutating case; it sets a meta key no reflect surfaces.

cases.name: update-agent-shape
cases.note: The record rides UNDER `agent`; the bare record rust and swift used to answer left a caller branching on `updated` reading nothing for the call that succeeded. FIRST and idempotent — see `_order`.

cases.name: unknown-agent
cases.note: Names the live ids in `agents` so a caller that guessed can correct; only `reason` is asserted, because the id list is fixture-dependent.

cases.name: kernel-verb-refusal
cases.note: `parent_id` is REQUIRED on create_agent (#23) — it used to be accepted and silently stripped while the addressed agent became the parent.

cases.name: reflect-kernel
cases.note: pairwise:false — the reply is checked for SHAPE on every transport but never byte-diffed. The distilled `tree` is VIEWER-DEPENDENT: `reflect` is gated like every other verb, so each node is asked only if the CALLER may reflect it, and a transport leg (an agent) legitimately sees fewer nodes than the in-proc operator (ungated). Same reason the origin-scoped `ledger` is pairwise:false. Before 2026-09-02 the roster walk dispatched `reflect` directly, so any caller allowed to reflect ONE agent read every descendant's sentence out of the tree.

cases.name: ledger-answers-everywhere
cases.note: pairwise:false — the reply is checked for SHAPE on every transport but never byte-diffed. `ledger` is ORIGIN-SCOPED by design (each leg sees the executions IT originated) and history accumulates between legs. The first ledger-all run proved it: the ws leg's view diverged from the operator's, correctly.

cases.name: no-verb-at-all
cases.note: A payload without `type` is not a send: every runtime refuses it in the launch phase (missing_arg on payload.type) for every sender, operator included — never a TypeError, never an `unhandled` from the target (measured 2026-09-02).

cases.name: create-empty-id
cases.note: A SUPPLIED id is the caller's choice and is validated as one; only an ABSENT id is minted. `""` used to be silently replaced by a minted id in rust/swift.

cases.name: delete-unknown
cases.note: A typo does not delete anything, and says so with a code plus the live `agents` index to correct from. Rust and swift answered a bare `{error: "no agent ..."}` — no code to branch on, no ids to recover with.

cases.name: kernel-verb-on-child
cases.note: Kernel verbs act on the TREE, so the agent named is the OPERAND, not the actor — every runtime refuses them at a non-root agent with `not_here` AND names the misaddressed verb in `verb`, which the ports used to omit.
